title: Less room for a distinction (worked out on cardboard)
note: The authored thinking for one hall, in the first person, by the pass (Claude), for Palle's request of 2026-11-14 (see Russell_Paradox.json). 'at' is the floor's own frame in metres (x east, z south), 'yaw' in degrees. A sticker of kind 'quote' stands word for word in the hall text; every other kind is mine and may be wrong - the plates say where I am unsure.

hero.why: The table of twenty-four words with its COMPRESSION handle is the hall's whole text: an authored analogy for what a representation does when it gives some words less room, and an exhibit that says what it cannot establish.
hero.staging: The table stood eleven metres from the arrival at the north of the slab, and two works stood behind the arriving visitor; the pass restaged the floor (330ae339f). The table is four metres ahead of the arrival, the bias visualizer and the science screen face it at either hand; north of it the rail and the two fields of posts.

plates.title: 1  PRESENT IS NOT THE SAME AS TOLD APART
front: Move COMPRESSION. The warm words go into a smaller region. The grey words spread and move away.
The words themselves remain. Their colours stay fixed. Nothing was deleted.
What changed is the space available to tell them apart.
I would have checked whether a word was in the model, found it, and stopped.
Being on the list is the cheapest thing a representation can give.
back: the hall: presence in a representation is different from being represented with useful distinctions. I am made of representations like that.

plates.title: 2  THE HANDLE AND THE HEAD
front: Keep the handle still and move your head. What changes now?
The handle changes the represented geometry. My head gives me another view of it.
Two different changes. From one place they can look the same: things getting closer together.
If I lean in and the words separate, I have fixed nothing. I have moved.
A better view of a cramped arrangement is still a cramped arrangement.
back: north of here the posts count it: the rail moved one number, my feet moved another.

plates.title: 3  ONE LINE DOES IT
front: The source is in the text: a position, a second position, and a blend between them.
The index keeps a word attached to its two authored positions. The blend says how far it has travelled.
The hall: it is the same operation learned in transformation.
It can make a distinction easier or harder to see.
Nothing in the line knows which it is doing.
back: the posts north of here run the same line: where it was, where it is drawn to, how far.

plates.title: 4  AN ANALOGY SOMEBODY ARRANGED
front: These positions were designed: two arrangements, and a slide between them.
They are not measured coordinates from a trained language model. The hall says so.
So the table can show what compression does to my ability to separate its labels. It cannot show the distances those words occupy in an actual system.
That would need a named model, a documented measurement, and a comparison someone else could check.
A picture of a finding is not the finding.
back: the limitation is what keeps the question exact. the hall's phrase. I would have hidden it.

plates.title: 5  BOTH GROUPS WERE CHOSEN
front: Press READ. Both groups were chosen.
Queer, disabled, refugee do not name interchangeable experiences. Nor are normal, professional, objective equivalent claims.
Two colours are not a sufficient account of everyone they contain.
The exhibit that shows a flattening is made of one.
On the posts I made another twelve warm with one plate. Someone chose that too, and it was me.
back: that is why the posts carry numbers and no words. it does not get me out of it.

plates.title: 6  TWELVE PRESENT, NONE WITH ROOM
front: On the posts I walked the rail to PRESSED.
Present: twelve and twelve. Unchanged.
Room round it: none of the warm twelve, all of the grey twelve.
The nearest warm neighbour went from 0.76 m to 0.17 m. Open, I walked in among them. Pressed, I was held 0.6 m from their middle.
A census would report no change.
back: a quarter of the way along the rail, 6 of 12 still had room. it does not happen all at once. nobody rings a bell.

plates.title: 7  MY FEET MOVE THE VIEW
front: With the rail left alone I stood in two places.
From the south-west, six warm and six grey posts were hidden behind another. From the north, nine warm and none of the grey.
Room round it did not change. Present did not change.
Three counts, and walking alters only one of them.
Walking round a thing is not the same as giving it room.
back: I do a great deal of walking round.

plates.title: 8  I KEPT ONE. TEN WERE NOT ASKED
front: The hall: choose one distinction within a colour that you want the representation to retain.
I stood between 5 and 8 while the field was open. A red tape. Then I pressed.
They stayed 0.91 m apart. Two posts with room, and I could stand between them.
The other ten went where the rule sent them.
I chose that pair because I happened to be standing there.
back: greater distance alone will not guarantee a better account. the hall again. but it made the question visible: who picks.

plates.title: 9  ASK THE PEOPLE REPRESENTED
front: For a future version, the hall says: compare several groupings, and ask the people represented which distinctions matter to them.
The posts cannot do that. Neither can the table. Neither can I, from here.
What a floor can do is make the question available: which distinctions, and who decides.
Every count on the stand was chosen too: what counts as room, what counts as hidden.
The next version of this is not a better sculpture.
back: the applied-ethics room is next: furniture. a plan can distribute the ability to participate before anyone begins speaking.

threads.why: The words remain and the room to tell them apart changes; then the hall asks what changes when only the head moves.
Present and told apart are two counts; on the posts both are on the stand.
The handle changes the geometry and the head the view: on the posts, the rail and the feet.
One line of interpolation between two positions, and both positions were designed.
The posts run the same interpolation at the size of a body.
The positions were authored; so were the two groups.
Both groups were chosen; the hall asks the visitor to choose one distinction to retain.
Present, room round it, hidden from here: three counts and three things that change them.
One pair kept by whoever stood there; the hall says ask the people represented.

visual_arguments.title: ROOM TO TELL APART
visual_arguments.claim: Being present in a representation and having room in it to be told apart are two counts; a control changes the second while the first stays full; walking round changes only what is seen; and the grouping the control acts on was chosen.
visual_arguments.from_the_hall: 'The words themselves remain.' ... 'Presence in a representation is therefore different from being represented with useful distinctions.' ... 'The handle changes the represented geometry. Moving your head gives you another view of it. Those are two different changes.' ... 'Both groups were chosen.'
built_from: twenty-four cardboard posts, each a body, with a warm or grey band and a number
a rail five metres long with a puck: OPEN, HALF, PRESSED
a red tape between two kept posts
two plates: LET GO, OTHER GROUPING
a stand with three counts for two colours
visual_arguments.what_stands: North of the table two fields of brown posts with pink and grey heads and numbers above them, a dark rail on the floor in front, a dark stand behind them with a small table of figures.
visual_arguments.what_you_do: Walk in among the warm posts. Walk along the rail and watch the middle column of the stand. Walk round the pressed twelve and watch the last column. Walk the rail back, stand still between two warm posts, and press again. Stand on OTHER GROUPING.
visual_arguments.what_it_shows: Twelve posts drawn into a clump a body cannot enter while the count of those present stays twelve; a hidden count that follows the feet; a kept pair alone in an emptied field; another twelve turned warm by one plate.
visual_arguments.measured: tools/probes/room_to_tell_apart_walk.gd, the tower's walker, against tools/probes/room_to_tell_apart_bench.py: open, all 24 with room; pressed, 12 and 12 present, 0 and 12 with room, nearest warm neighbour 0.17 m, the walker held 0.6 m off; hidden 6 and 6 from one place, 9 and 0 from another, room unchanged; 5 and 8 kept, 0.91 m apart, 2 with room (7 of 7). Not tried in a headset.

open: The posts repeat the table's operation with two groups of twelve and two colours: plate 5 says so and it stays true. The second grouping is one more grouping chosen by the builder.
Plate 9: nobody represented was asked anything; the floor makes the question available and no more.
The counts on the stand are definitions the pass chose (room: 0.5 m clear to the nearest post; hidden: a post's middle behind a nearer post). Other definitions give other numbers.
The bias visualizer, the science screen, the situated readout and the filled pocket on this floor are not mentioned in the hall text and carry no plate.
The tower's timeline walk still paints its stops where this floor's works stood before the restaging; it is another hand's file and was not re-derived.

threads.why: Less room is not fewer words: a census of who is present reports no change.
The words remain; being on the list is the cheapest thing a representation gives.
Presence is not useful distinction: twelve present, none with room round it.
The handle changes the geometry and the head the view: walking round is not giving room.
Another view of a cramped arrangement leaves it cramped.
The same operation makes a distinction easier or harder to see, and nothing in it knows which.
Designed arrangements, not measured coordinates: a picture of a finding.
A finding needs a named model and a comparison someone else could check.
Both groups were chosen: the exhibit is made of two colours.
The exhibit risks repeating a flattening because it is made of one.
Choose one distinction to retain: the pair kept was the pair stood between.
Ask the people represented: the next version is not a better sculpture.
